survivors.claim: The AC-4 test cites ADR-0017 in its header comment and its assert failure message, but the amendment record this build shipped is ADR-0018 (D7 was renumbered in the same build and the deviations sidecar says every mention was amended; these two were missed).
survivors.impact: When this pin ever fails, its message sends the reader to the wrong amendment record.
survivors.evidence: grep -n ADR-0017 tests/mocks/review-page.test.js yields line 140 (header comment: ADR-0017 clause (a) breadcrumb) and line 155 (assert message: ADR-0017 clause a). docs/adr/0018-the-review-page-departs-from-its-spec.md is the record; 0017 is the shadcn register ADR.

survivors.claim: AC-20260912-06-2 carries the worked literal 2 open items block approval, which is false for the AC-1 fixture (isOpen counts the addressed note, true total 3); the test correctly pins 3, but unlike AC-9 (D9a) and AC-10 (D10a) the AC text was left unamended, so the spec now carries a parenthetical its own passing test contradicts.
survivors.impact: A reader checking the spec against the test sees a number the test never asserts and has to find the sidecar to learn why.
survivors.evidence: Spec lines 131-132: name the same total it counts (2 open items block approval). tests/mocks/review-page.test.js:103-104 asserts trueOpenTotal computed from baseNotes(open).filter(status !== resolved) = 3 (deviations sidecar bullet 1 records the same). Executed: node --test tests/mocks/review-page.test.js, AC-2 passes with 3.

survivors.claim: The Contracts block promises parseFlatDom nodes expose textContent, but the promoted helper exposes no text reader at all (D5 says unchanged except for one addition, so the Contract line is the overclaim); as a consequence review-page.test.js grows four raw-HTML readers (rawText, cellText, rawInnerText, sliceCrumb) that regex the served bytes to recover element text.
survivors.impact: The shared helper documents a surface wider than what it delivers, and every future review-page test will re-invent the same text-scraping workaround instead of calling one shim method.
survivors.evidence: Spec Contracts line 80 lists textContent among the node members. grep -n textContent tests/helpers.js returns nothing. tests/mocks/review-page.test.js lines 78-79 say: The flat-DOM shim (tests/helpers.js) exposes no textContent reader. Four raw-HTML helpers at review-page.test.js lines 80, 120, 158, 165; the three-or-more duplication calibration in .claude/rules/spec-pipeline.md Review Checks names the extraction.

survivors.claim: An assert failure message in the AC-6 test embeds a calendar date (the 2026-09-11 expiry sweep), which the tests convention says test citations never carry.
survivors.impact: A dated narrative in a failure message ages into noise the next time the file is read.
survivors.evidence: .claude/rules/conventions/tests.md: never dates, people, hosts, versions, or prior behavior. review-browser.test.js lines 104-105: it was orphaned scaffolding the 2026-09-11 expiry sweep deleted the test() body of but not the helper itself.

killed.claim: D3 server-side project count (scope === project) could disagree with the recount() bucket (rows with no data-label), e.g. a ledger question with no screen.
killed.evidence: review-page.js:305 filters items to (scope === mock and labelSet.has(screen)) or scope === project before any render, and rowOpen (line 166) emits data-label only when scope === mock and screen is set. So the set of rows with no data-label is exactly the project-scope set; the two derivations are equal over every input the page can render. AC-2 test executed in both directions (1 without data-zero; 0 with data-zero): pass.

killed.claim: The new bare-class matcher in parseFlatDom scans the whole compound remainder, so an attribute value containing a dot would be misread as a class requirement and break a review.browser.js query.
killed.evidence: grep for q(...)/qa(...) selectors containing a dot in spec/scripts/lib/review.browser.js returns nothing: no selector in the script under test carries a dot inside a bracket value. Executed review-browser.test.js under vm over the real markup: 3/3 pass.
